conventions.convention: The normalized Hecke generators satisfy H_s² = 1 + (v⁻¹ − v)H_s; C_s = H_s + v. The spherical character is H_s ↦ v⁻¹ and the antispherical character is H_s ↦ −v. Both induced modules are right Hecke modules.
Hecke standard bases use left-minimal representatives {}^JW of W_Jw. Singular-block weights use right-minimal representatives W^J of wW_J. Inversion exchanges these representative sets.

In the singular-block definition, W_μ denotes the dot stabilizer W_J, not the integral-reflection group bearing the same notation in its published supplier. For integral μ, the latter group is all of W. The dot action is w·μ = w(μ + ρ) − ρ, and μ is dot-antidominant.

The classical polynomial parameter is q = v⁻². The shifted canonical coefficients define M^J_{y,x}(q) = v^{ℓ(y)−ℓ(x)}m_{y,x} and N^J_{y,x}(q) = v^{ℓ(y)−ℓ(x)}n_{y,x}. Spherical is Deodhar's u = −1 family and antispherical is his u = q family, with inverted indices.

Parabolic category O is the genuine full subcategory of ordinary O consisting of locally U(p_J)-finite objects. Its standards are generalized Vermas induced from finite-dimensional Levi simples with the positive radical acting trivially; costandards are their restricted duals.

The regular parabolic multiplicity theorem assumes a dominant regular integral type-A base λ and left-minimal labels. In the antidominant base w₀·λ, the same weight has longest-left label yw₀; its shortest-left encoding a = w_Jyw₀ represents the weight (w_Ja)·(w₀·λ). Reindexing does not replace matrix entries by n_{a,b}(1).
The character matrix N has rows indexed by generalized standards and columns by simples, so the column-vector equation is M = NL. Its inverse gives simple characters by rows, with support y ≥ x.
Category-O structural and multiplicity assertions retain the Axiom of Choice inherited from their published prerequisites; the finite Hecke-module constructions use no choice principle.

load_bearing.statement: Assuming AC, genuine parabolic category O has the stated Levi-dominant simples and generalized standards, a largest locally finite quotient functor carrying ordinary projectives to parabolic projectives, and enough projectives and injectives. In a fixed integral block, projectives have finite generalized-standard flags and labelled standard quotients with higher-standard kernels; generalized-standard/simple classes are Grothendieck bases, characters are injective, BGG reciprocity holds, and restricted duality and standard-costandard Ext¹ vanishing hold.
For all x,y ∈ {}^JW, n_{y,x} = Σ_{z∈W_J}(−1)^{ℓ(z)}v^{ℓ(z)}p_{zy,x}. If W_J is finite with longest element w₀^J, then m_{y,x} = p_{w₀^Jy,w₀^Jx}.

Assuming AC and the regular antidominant-to-facet data, T sends every labelled standard and costandard to its μ-labelled counterpart. TL(w·λ) = L(w·μ) for w ∈ W^J and is zero otherwise. The translate Ξ_μ of L(−ρ) is the projective-injective cover P(μ), with every distinct singular standard occurring once.

For each x ∈ {}^JW there are unique bar-fixed C_x ∈ m_x + Σ_{y<x}vZ[v]m_y and D_x ∈ n_x + Σ_{y<x}vZ[v]n_y. These families are A-bases of their respective modules. No coefficientwise positivity is asserted.

Assuming AC, a dominant regular integral type-A base λ and x,y ∈ {}^JW, [Δ^J(y·λ):L(x·λ)] = (P^J(x·λ):Δ^J(y·λ)) = Σ_{u∈W_J}(−1)^{ℓ(u)}P_{uy,x}(1) = n_{y,x}(1). The supplying character identity is ch Δ^J(y·λ) = Σ_{u∈W_J}(−1)^{ℓ(u)}ch Δ(uy·λ).
Assuming AC and the stated type-A facet data, for y,w ∈ W^J, [M(y·μ):L(w·μ)] = (P(w·μ):Δ(y·μ)) = P_{yw₀,ww₀}(1) = m_{k(y),k(w)}(1), where k(w) = w₀^Jw⁻¹w₀ ∈ {}^JW. This is the spherical family.

Assuming AC and the stated integral antidominant regular-to-facet data, if γ is a weight of the translating finite-dimensional simple E and w′·μ = w·λ + γ, then w′·μ = w·μ and γ = w(μ−λ). Consequently E ⊗ Δ(w·λ) has exactly one Verma factor of central character χ_μ, namely Δ(w·μ), once.

concerns.concern: Fact [F5] locates the ordinary triangular construction at 'steps 1.1--3.2' of thm-existence-and-uniqueness-of-the-kazhdan-lusztig-basis. That published item's current proof has only steps 1.1 and 2.1 and delegates the elementary construction to lem-type-a-kazhdan-lusztig-basis-has-elementary-triangular-bar-properties. The locator is stale. The assigned theorem independently supplies the full triangular induction in its own steps 1.1–5.1, so this does not undermine its proof.

alerts.finding: Step 2.2 says, 'The singular ordinary multiplicity theorem of [F3] has exactly these indices for the sorted-entry stabilizer,' referring to P_{d(C)w₀,d(A)w₀}(1). Its Statement and step 1.1 explicitly make d(A) = w_A⁻¹ minimal LEFT modulo K, whereas thm-singular-category-o-multiplicities-are-parabolic-kl-polynomials accepts minimal RIGHT labels. The tuple identity a(A) = b d(A), with b sorted, gives actual singular weight label w_A = d(A)⁻¹. The desired coefficient is recoverable: apply the supplier to w_C,w_A, then simultaneous inversion and conjugation by w₀ give P_{w_Cw₀,w_Aw₀} = P_{d(C)w₀,d(A)w₀}. This bridge is implicit; the assertion that the supplier has exactly the displayed input indices omits its representative-side hypothesis.

seams_checked.note: The singular theorem quotes the regular dominant-base formula P_{y,w}(1) and explicitly converts its antidominant labels by right multiplication by w₀. The regular parabolic theorem retains the regular ambient central-character hypothesis and dominant left-minimal labels. The regular-to-regular translation citation preserves labelled standards, simples and projectives and imports no grading.

The structural uses retain genuine locally parabolic-finite category O, finite integral central summands, generalized-standard flags, reciprocity and duality. The polynomial consumer distinguishes the entry stabilizer from the column Levi and spherical from antispherical coefficients. Its step 2.2 nevertheless calls left-minimal inverse labels 'exactly' the singular supplier's indices, although that supplier requires right-minimal labels. The numerical formula survives the elementary inversion/conjugation bridge recorded in the alert.
